A three-phase, 24-month roadmap | PHASE 1 · Months 0–6 | Assess & stabilise | Baseline scorecard and data inventory | Governance committee; a data steward per unit | Core KPI framework and data dictionary v1 | Quick win: PRO pipeline dashboard | M6  Governance charter and KPIs approved | PHASE 2 · Months 6–15 | Standardise & integrate | One PRO data model: application to retention | Central data store with automated quality checks | Data-sharing agreements updated with partners | Automated monthly and quarterly reporting | M15  Integrated data and automated reports live | PHASE 3 · Months 15–24 | Embed & scale | Evaluation framework: retention and community outcomes | Self-serve dashboards; tiered data-literacy training | Ready for +50 ITPs/yr and the Francophone stream | Re-assess maturity; set the next 2-year plan | M24  Maturity re-assessed and next plan set | Dependencies:  executive sponsor and governance charter before Phase 2  ·  partner data-sharing agreements before integration  ·  analyst capacity and tooling budget before Phase 3 | 5

Key risks and how we manage them | RISK | RATING | MITIGATION | Capacity and competing priorities | High | Phase the work; quick wins first; protect analyst time; share load with stewards | Privacy and data-sharing limits across partners | High | Privacy impact assessments; start agreement updates in Phase 1; collect minimum necessary data | Low adoption or resistance | Medium | Co-design with units; champions; build into existing workflows; show time saved | Legacy systems and fragmented data | Medium | Data model and dictionary before tools; integrate step by step; stay vendor-neutral | Shifting policy, funding or scope | Medium | Governance committee sets priorities; 6-month review gates; tie to Ministry reporting | 7

Appendix: maturity levels defined | Used in the Step 1 scorecard; adapted from the CMMI Data Management Maturity model and DAMA-DMBOK | 1 | Initial | Ad hoc and person-dependent. Data sits in personal spreadsheets, terms mean different things to different teams, and reports are rebuilt by hand. | AT TOUCHSTONE | Each team keeps its own candidate tracker; "placed" is counted differently across units. | 2 | Managed | Basic, repeatable practices within teams. Key datasets have known owners and some documentation, but standards differ between units. | AT TOUCHSTONE | Units use set intake templates and produce a regular report, each in their own way. | 3 | Defined | Organisation-wide standards. A governance committee, data stewards, a shared data dictionary and agreed KPIs apply across all units. | AT TOUCHSTONE | One definition of "placed" and "retained"; a named data steward in every unit. | 4 | Measured | Data quality and use are tracked against targets. Data is integrated, quality checks are automated, and leaders use dashboards routinely. | AT TOUCHSTONE | Application-to-retention data in one store; completeness tracked against a 95% target. | 5 | Optimised | Continuous improvement. Evaluation and predictive analytics shape strategy, and feedback loops refine processes over time. | AT TOUCHSTONE | Retention findings inform candidate–site matching and recruitment for new streams. | 10
